source_encoding: ASCII, verified by strict decoding; source bytes retained unchanged
paper_citation: F.G. Kondev, M. Wang, W.J. Huang, S. Naimi, and G. Audi, The NUBASE2020 evaluation of nuclear physics properties, Chinese Physics C 45, 030001 (2021), DOI 10.1088/1674-1137/abddae.
paper_boundary_pinpoint: Publisher PDF page 030001-2, Introduction; data available to the authors, not every reference's publication or discovery year.
cutoff_distinction: The paper's availability boundary is retained separately from this downloaded ASCII revision. The ASCII contains one discovery-year field of 2021. It must not be silently described as a dataset whose every year field is at most 2020. A reported discovery year alone does not establish when data became available to the authors or prove an update beyond the paper's boundary.

license_scope_note: The published work explicitly carries CC BY 3.0. The official companion ASCII header gives its paper citation but no separate license notice. This archive retains attribution to that work and distinguishes the confirmed publication license from an independently stated ASCII-file license.
transformations: Fixed-width raw slices and byte locations preserved; conservative decimal-string/property parsing added; uncertainty operators and units retained; unknown tokens and systematics markers not discarded; no scientific values recalculated.
completeness_scope: All 5843 source state records and every source byte in this specific downloaded NUBASE2020 ASCII file are accounted for. This is not all excited nuclear levels, all nuclear species known in 2026, all future species, or proof of physical preparation or material enablement.
observation_status_policy: No per-state existence/observation classification is inferred from #, blank fields, discovery year, or presence in the table; such classification requires the underlying evaluation and relevant source evidence.
distribution_recommendation: Preserve the small original ASCII, schema, metadata, parser and independent verifier. The large generated normalized JSON is optional and can be reconstructed in memory for offline verification.
